To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the glutaminolysis-derived carbon and nitrogen flux are predominantly directed to gluconeogenesis in periportal hepatocyte and to ureogenesis in the downstream region of the liver acinus.
glutamine-derived ureogenesis in periportal cells is not faster than that in the whole liver.

the zonation of glutamine-derived nitrogen metabolism is not as pronounced as the zonation of the glutamine carbon metabolism and that the zonation pattern of ureogenesis is not as pronounced and uniform as the zonation pattern found in gluconeogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the zonation of carbon fluxes and the nitrogen fluxes in glutamine metabolism.
the elucidation of metabolic zonation in the liver.
the investigation of the metabolic zonation and heterogeneity in the liver parenchymal cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ureogenesis from glutamate and glutamine is not a periportal phenomenon.
glutaminase activity does not predetermine the zonation of glutamine-derived ureogenesis.
the zonal heterogeneity in glutamine metabolism is not only determined by the zonation of the glutamine-degrading enzyme but also by the zonation in ureogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glutamine metabolism is not uniformly distributed over the liver acinus, but that ureogenesis is.
the zonation of glutamine and ammonia metabolism in the liver is more complex than previously thought.
the liver acinus is a highly dynamic system in which carbon and nitrogen flux are not only determined by the metabolic zonation but are also regulated by the concentration of ammonia in the blood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carbon and nitrogen flow through glutamine metabolism are not the same in the different regions of the liver acinus.
the zonation of glutamine and ammonia metabolism is not the same and that the zonation is dependent on the ammonia concentration in the portal blood.
the proportions between the carbon flux and the nitrogen fluxes in the periportal cells are different along the liver acinar axis.
